predecessors.name: Han dynasty
predecessors.text: the Ji Province core (Julu, Wei) and Wancheng in Nanyang taken in March 184; Runan-Yingchuan was fought over but not held

successors.name: Cao Cao
successors.text: the Taihang Mountains, where the Heishan bandits 'operated as a bandit confederacy' with access to Henei and the provinces of Bing, Ji and Yan

capitals.name: Guangzong (Zhang Jue's base, not a capital)

ledger.x: 184: Zhang Jue raises the Yellow Turbans.
184: Bo Cai and Peng Tuo are defeated at Yangzhai and Xihua; the Yu Province front is closed within the year.
185: PAGE SILENT on when the Heishan took any ground.
185: the Ji Province core is lost.
188: the Yellow Turbans rise again in Qing and Xu.
192: the Qing rebels move on Yan and are broken.
205: the last Yellow Turban remnant submits.

wars.name: Yellow Turban Rebellion
wars.outcome: The first rising was crushed by February 185: Zhang Jue died of illness, Zhang Liang and Zhang Bao were killed; Bo Cai and Zhang Mancheng were beaten in the south.

wars.name: Qingzhou Yellow Turban revolt
wars.outcome: The Qing and Xu rebels moved into Yan Province in 192 and over 300,000 surrendered to Cao Cao at Jibei.

wars.name: Heishan bandits and the Taihang remnant
wars.outcome: Zhang Yan's confederacy was broken by Yuan Shao in 193 and surrendered to Cao Cao in summer 205 with 100,000 followers.

certainty.note: No page gives a rebel frontier; every shape is a cluster of named places, never a treaty or survey line.
